output.summary: A biennial vegetable known only from cultivation, with no known wild ancestral form; its geographic origin is uncertain and domestication likely occurred in West or Central Asia. It forms a layered bulb below a fan of hollow bluish-green leaves, and bulb swelling is triggered by day length. The bulb and young plants are eaten raw, cooked or pickled, while chopping can release eye-irritating chemicals.
output.edibilityNote: Mature bulbs and young whole plants are eaten raw or cooked; bulbs are also pickled or made into chutneys.
